# The development lifecycle

## Ask the index first

**Before making any decision, ALWAYS check if the index can answer first. Before searching with any tool (e.g., PowerShell, grep, sed, awk, etc), ALWAYS see if the index can answer first. Anything the index misses gets recorded as a miss and presented back to the user as a potential index improvement.**

Ask with `mise run graph:ask -- find <the problem in your own words>`, then read an entry with `mise run graph:ask -- read <ID>`. Report what it answered weakly with `mise run graph:ask -- misses --near`, and record a gap with `mise run graph:ask -- gap`.

The index answers from these, among others:

- `STD` entries of project lattice, standard
- `PRI` entries of project lattice, principle
- `PAT` entries of project lattice, pattern
- `MEC` entries of project lattice, mechanism
- `CAP` entries of project lattice, capability
- `TD` entries of project lattice, debt
- `PDD` entries of project lattice, pending-decision
- `BL` entries of project lattice, backlog
- `ADR` entries of project lattice, decision
- `TSD` entries of project lattice, discovery
- `TSDQ` entries of project lattice, discovery
- `LGQ` entries of project lattice, question

This skill's tasks span the activities delivery, planning-and-estimation, release-and-versioning, acceptance, regression-testing, continuous-integration, technical-debt-management, architecture-decision-making and documentation, and a task often needs several of them, named together and separated by commas. Read each row's flags and the line under it, where an entry's boundary, its successor and the debt against it are named.

The always-on rules are in `AGENTS.md`. This skill is the procedure behind them.

Paths are relative to the LATTICE repository, browsable at <https://github.com/nebularis/lattice>.

## Starting a named unit of work

Read, in order:

1. the accepted decisions it depends on, in `docs/architecture/decisions/`
2. its plan, `docs/developer/plans/<unit>.md`
3. its status record, `docs/developer/status/<unit>.md`, the one authoritative live state
4. any open review request, `docs/developer/review/<unit>-review.md`

Do not treat a plan as a status log.

Do not move a path before its ADR and path manifest are approved.

## The documents

Only plans and status records are mandatory. Every unit has a plan and a status record. Every other document below is optional, and a project that keeps none of them still keeps these two. Every location is a default, and a project overrides it in its `skill_values`.

| Document | Holds | Changes when |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/developer/sketches/<unit>.md` | the broad shape of an idea, its options and questions | freely. Usually deleted once a plan replaces it |
| `docs/developer/plans/<unit>.md` | scope, dependencies, steps, decisions, planned validation | only when the plan changes |
| `docs/developer/status/<unit>.md` | live state, next action, history | after every material action, result, blocker or handoff |
| `docs/developer/review/<unit>-review.md` | the review request: scope, artefacts, exact commands, pass criteria, open questions, a link to the status record | before handoff. Closed after disposition |
| `docs/developer/validation/<slice-id>.md` | a slice's Validation Pack | written with the slice, results filled at verification |
| `docs/developer/pending-design-decisions.md` | design decisions that matter but cannot be made yet, with the options known | add when raised, remove naming the decision record, sketch or plan that settles it |
| `docs/developer/technical-debt.md` | debt with no planned home: a shortcut, a gap between a claim and the behaviour, a check that does not run | add when spotted, remove naming the plan that takes it on. Never features, follow-ups or deferred slices |
| `docs/developer/INDEX.md` | the generated register of every unit and every slice, written by `mise run build:work` from the status records | never by hand. Regenerated in the same commit as the record it reads |

Never create a second status record for a unit.

In LATTICE, leave legacy sketches alone until the maintainer reviews them. `docs/developer/` itself holds the registers and durable guidance only. `docs/developer/INDEX.md` is regenerated in the same commit as the record it reads (STD-305).

## Recording what we learn

A learning that outlives its session goes into a register in the same change that produced it, and the index is refreshed so other agents can find it. A learning left in a commit message is lost.

**Update the registers and the skills of the domains, and add your project's own.** A domain's registers and skills are shared by every project that uses it, so a learning that holds beyond this project goes there and not only here. What a tool, store or platform actually does goes to the register of the domain about it, as the next row with its Evidence cell, which says what was run and on which version. A rule an agent needs to do a task well goes into the domain's skill for that task, and a rule only this project needs goes into this project's own register, or into its additions to the skill (`.vyvid/skills/<domain>/<skill>.md`). A project adds its own registers and rules to the domain's, and never works around one it disagrees with without recording why.

**Which register takes it.**

| What was learned | Goes in |
|---|---|
| what a store, tool, engine or platform actually does, found by probing or being surprised | the discovery register of the domain it is about, as the next row. Otherwise the unit's status record until a register owns it |
| a choice made, where a decision record is warranted | a decision record, drafted as Proposed |
| a choice that matters and cannot be made yet | `docs/developer/pending-design-decisions.md` |
| a shortfall in something that exists, with no planned home | `docs/developer/technical-debt.md` |
| an answer the repository holds and no register entry does, found by falling back from the index | the register that should hold it, in the same change. Otherwise `docs/developer/technical-debt.md`, and tell the maintainer |
| a rule about how we write, name, structure or check something | the skill that an agent reads for that task, not a commit message |
| a cost measured, with numbers | the discovery record, citing the benchmark |

**How to write the entry.** One bolded lead sentence stating the claim, then the detail. The index extracts that sentence as the claim and never stores a second copy, so an entry whose first sentence is a preamble indexes as a preamble. Keep it under 200 characters and state the cost as well as the benefit.

**Then refresh the index.**

```bash
mise run build:knowledge
mise run check:identifiers
```

The first derives the index again so the entry is findable. The second fails if the entry cites an identifier that resolves to nothing, which is the commonest way a new entry is wrong.

A learning left in a commit message is lost: 22 of this project's learnings existed only in git history when the index was built, including a Windows newline translation that silently corrupted generated SPARQL and two merge resolutions that made a task skip test modules without failing. The index is built as [ADR-A134](../../../docs/architecture/decisions/ADR-A134-knowledge-index-and-design-shape-vocabulary.md) says.

These rows are LATTICE's.

| What was learned | Goes in |
|---|---|
| what a store, tool, engine or platform actually does, found by probing or being surprised | [`docs/architecture/triple-store-discovery.md`](../../../docs/architecture/triple-store-discovery.md) as the next `TSD-`*n*, for a store. Otherwise the unit's status record until a register owns it |
| a facet value an entry needs and the scheme lacks | a project facets file named by `facets` in `vyvid.toml`, as a row with Ratified no, or Вивід's general scheme through its side. Tag the entry with it in the same change |
| a rule a skill states, so the index can rank it | the standard register, as a row whose Pointer is the skill's section, with Ratified no |

The row for an answer found by falling back from the index is STD-272. For a store, the next row of the discovery record is the next `TSD-`*n*.

**A register's header is a title, its Unit type line and at most one line of state.** A column's meaning is the `rdfs:comment` of the T-Box property it maps to, written once, so a header explaining its columns restates it. `check:knowledge` fails a register holding a table whose first column is not `ID` or `#`.

The first takes about two seconds.

## Epics, phases, slices and milestones

A project's configuration can rename these units and the words of the ladder below. These are the defaults.

| Unit | Is | Ends with | Documents |
|---|---|---|---|
| Epic | a large package spanning phases, marked as an epic in its record | never. Only its phases end | epic plan, phase plans, epic status |
| Phase | slices that together give a demonstrable capability | a phase gate: milestone, docs updated, decisions ratified | phase plan and status |
| Slice | one agent work package, independently reviewable and testable | the validation gate | its Validation Pack |
| Milestone | an end-to-end outcome in the local stack | a demo and a green end-to-end suite | the phase plan and status |

No epic-level review is created until every phase plan exists and every acceptance suite passes.

**Slice sizing.** More than about 15 test cases, or more than two modules touched, splits the slice. Fewer than 3 merges it. Skeleton slices, with one build smoke test, are exempt.

**Every slice delivers:**

1. code in one or two modules
2. a Validation Pack with the invariant it protects (one paragraph, citing the decisions or gaps), a test table (ID, Given/When/Then, level L0 to L8, invariant, pass criterion, positive or negative), **one command** that runs everything, the artefacts to inspect, and deliberate non-coverage with the slice that covers it
3. its row on the home unit's slice board moved to `built`, and `mise run build:work` run, so docs/developer/INDEX.md's register follows
4. the doc delta, in the same slice. No "docs later"

**The validation gate.** The maintainer reviews the Validation Pack before running anything, runs the one command and inspects the artefacts. An adversarial probe follows: the maintainer names a test, or leaves the pick to the agent, and the agent breaks the implementation, shows the test fails, restores it, and records each probe and its result in the status record. The maintainer's merge is the sign-off. There is no separate sign-off log.

**Test levels.** L0 build smoke, L1 unit, L2 property and determinism, L3 contract, L4 component integration, L5 system end-to-end, L6 UI end-to-end, L7 non-functional, L8 hostile and security. A project's configuration can replace this scale.

**Non-weakening.** No slice deletes, skips or loosens an earlier slice's test without a decision-record-grade justification in its Validation Pack, countersigned at the gate.

In LATTICE an epic is marked `Unit type: Epic`. `docs/developer/validation/LOG.md` is retired (2026-10-10). A justification for weakening an earlier slice's test is ADR-grade.

## Picking up and finishing

The slice board of a unit's status record is the one place a slice's state is written, and `mise run work:board` reads it from the tip of every local and remote branch. The board's shape is fixed.

```markdown
| Slice | Deliverable | State | Blocked on |
|---|---|---|---|
| ABC-1b.3b | aggregate bindings | building 2026-10-30, briefed 2026-10-27 | |
| ABC-1b.4 | qualifying rules | planned | ABC-1b.3 |
```

- **A slice's state is written once, on the board of its home unit**, the unit whose plan defines it. An agent that builds a slice of one unit on another unit's branch sets the row in the home unit's record, on that branch. The adopting unit's record says so in its history and never carries a second row.
- **Mark before you touch.** Picking up is one edit, and it is the first edit: set the row to `building <day>`, add a history line, run `mise run build:work`, and commit the mark alone, so the board sees the claim from the first push. An agent caught editing unmarked stops, marks and commits the mark before going on. A unit or a plan picked up whole is its record's `**Status:**` line changed the same way.
- **A state is a word of the ladder and the day it was reached.** `planned`, `briefed`, `building`, `built`, `verified`, `merged`, `tagged`, with `blocked` and `dropped` aside, dated from `building` on, newest first in the cell, so the cell is its own trail. The day is the fact written. The commit is read from git by `mise run work:board --commits`, never written.
- **A unit's state is its board's roll-up.** Where a record has a board, its `**Status:**` word and day are what the rows give: building while any row is building, dated by the earliest, else the lowest word of the rows at built or later, dated by the latest, else blocked if any row is, else the highest of planned and briefed. Dropped rows count only when every row is dropped. `mise run work:normalise -- --apply` sets the word, and the `work` check refuses one that disagrees. The board shows the trunk's state and each branch further on.
- **Handing off is one edit**, the row to `built <day>` in the commit that carries the Validation Pack's handoff. The maintainer's verification is `verified`, and the merge into `main` flips the rows it delivers to `merged <day>` in the merge commit.
- **A slice id is `PREFIX-segment(.segment)*`**, a segment being optional capitals, digits and one lowercase letter, and the prefix declared on the unit's plan's `**Prefix:**` line. `ABC-1b.3b`, `XYZ-2.6d`, `QRS-S1` and `UV-DOC1` are ids. A slice is defined by its row, and a slice a plan names with no row fails `mise run check:identifiers`.
- **No plan and no status record names a branch.** The board derives the branch from where it finds the row, and plans move between branches.
- **The register is regenerated in the same commit.** The `work` hook check refuses a commit whose touched records and docs/developer/INDEX.md's region disagree, or whose touched board is malformed, and names the task that fixes it.
- **Before the first edit in any checkout, run `mise run work:here`.** It writes your presence, `--role build`, `review` or `read` with `--model`, into the checkout's git-ignored local folder, and lists the sessions touched in the last twelve hours. Where another live session is building there, or you were asked to review, say who is here and ask the maintainer before writing. A reviewer's findings go to the review request or to chat, never into a file another live session is building.

Ask the board before reading branches. `mise run work:board` answers where every unit and slice is, with `--all` for every row, `--fetch` to fetch every remote first, `--measure` for each branch's content share on `main`, and `--commits` for the commit that set each printed row. docs/developer/INDEX.md holds the state of the tree it was built from, and `mise run graph:ask -- read <slice id>` prints a slice's row.

The work board is [ADR-A151](../../../docs/architecture/decisions/ADR-A151-the-work-board.md), plan `work-board`. A slice's state is written once, on the board of its home unit (STD-300), for example an agent that builds a CCS slice on a formal-methods branch sets the row in the CCS record, on that branch. Marking before touching is STD-301, the ladder is STD-302, the roll-up is STD-317, the slice id grammar is STD-303 with the ids `CCS-9b.3b`, `FMH-2.6d`, `AIR-S1` and `OD-DOC1`, no plan names a branch (STD-304), the register is regenerated in the same commit (STD-305), and presence is STD-306, written into `.local/agents/`. A board row in LATTICE reads `| CCS-9b.3b | aggregate bindings | building 2026-10-30, briefed 2026-10-27 | |` followed by `| CCS-9b.4 | qualifying rules | planned | CCS-9b.3 |`, the commit that set each row is read by `mise run work:board -- --commits`, and `mise run work:board -- --all`, `-- --fetch`, `-- --measure` and `-- --commits` pass the flags after the separator, with `graph:ask -- read <slice id>` printing a slice's row.

**ROADMAP.md is kept whole, section by section** (STD-307). It is the maintainer's summary, and every section is current or says why not.

| Section | Kept by | When |
|---|---|---|
| 1 the programme at a glance, 7 branches, 9 decisions waiting, 11 completed units | generated by `mise run build:roadmap`, which the post-merge hook runs on `main` | after every merge into `main`, and on demand. Never edited by hand |
| 2 how the epics depend on one another, 8 the critical path | the planner, as diagrams | when a plan's Dependencies section gains or loses a dependency between units, or a blocker on the board changes the longest chain |
| 3 the layers | the ontology author, as a diagram | when an ADR changes the substrate's import order or proposes a layer |
| 4 active epics, 6 the platform programme | the agent handing an epic or a phase off, one subsection per epic | at each handoff and each merge that moves the epic: its documents, its ADRs, what moved and what is next, in the same commit as the status record |
| 5 smaller units | nobody. It points at section 1 | never |
| 10 the maintainer's queue | the agent proposes an order at each handoff, the maintainer orders | at each handoff that changes what unblocks the most work |
| 12 observations | the agent that refreshes the roadmap | at each refresh, every observation checked and a stale one removed |

A handoff that changes a unit's state says in its report which roadmap sections it refreshed and which it left, and why. Where a hand-written section disagrees with section 1, section 1 is right and the section is refreshed.

## Building a slice

- **Brief before branch.** A slice is briefed on `main` (scene, questions, each option's consequences), and the maintainer answers before a branch is due. The maintainer creates the branch, from the current `main`, unless they say otherwise.
- **Examples first.** The first phase writes the examples the work must accept, and the maintainer commits them. The building phase follows.
- **Pause before commit.** The agent builds and verifies, writes the Validation Pack's handoff and results, updates the status record, and stops. The maintainer commits.
- **Report on the index at every handoff.** List the questions it answered weakly or not at all, the near answers and the gaps recorded while reading (`mise run graph:ask -- misses --near`). Say which entry, facet value, column or edge would have carried each, such as a Does not cover cell, a Distinguished from or Bears on id, or an addendum's Reverses lead, and add any answer the fallback found to its register in the same change. A gap is recorded with `mise run graph:ask -- gap` when it is found, not remembered at the end, and closed with `mise run graph:ask -- close <ID>` in the change that writes its signpost.
- **Executing a whole plan autonomously.** The request is the go-ahead to author every slice, but do not ratify decision records, record each open design decision in the status record rather than choosing silently, and never report a check as passed that could not run.
- **Estimates** are in tokens, not agent days, so they can be compared with actual cost afterwards.

Examples first is ADR-A-C2, and the knowledge index report at a handoff is STD-272.

## Merging and releasing

- **Merge before tag.** A release tag names a commit on `main`. The order is commit, merge into `main`, then tag. A tag on an unmerged branch can name a commit that never reaches `main`.
- **Branch from `main`**, so a branch starts from every merged release, unless the maintainer has said parallel work is under way.
- **Version bumps happen once, at merge, never mid-branch.** Nobody consumes a branch's version numbers before it merges, so bumping per slice re-pins files for no reader and still has to happen again at the merge. A branch's new or changed documents keep citing the version `main` was pinned to at the branch point throughout the branch's life. Expect the project's version check to report a pending bump for a branch's own changed content until the actual merge-time bump, which is the correct state of a branch mid-flight, not a defect to work around.
- **Versions on a working branch.** Where the maintainer has agreed that a branch defers versioning, the branch makes no bump, its status record says so, and the version check's unbumped report is expected there. The branch writes each change's release note when it makes the change, under an Unreleased heading. The bump is made once, before the merge into `main`, and the tags follow the merge.
- **Release tags are the maintainer's.** Whenever the release record gains a row, or the version check lists pending tags, end the handoff with a notice headed `🔴 RELEASE TAGS REQUIRED`, listing each tag as a, b, c with the commands to create and push them once the change is merged. Repeat it in every handoff until the tags exist.
- **Test suites before a merge, by convention, never in a hook.** A hook runs quick checks only. Before a branch is merged into `main`, run every suite the branch touched that the full check leaves out and the hooks never run, and the handoff that asks for the merge lists each with its result, or says it was not run and why. A failure on one engine or platform is recorded in the register that owns it and is fixed or accepted before the merge.
- **The merge gate.** A merge into `main` runs the hooks' merge checks. Before merging on the hosting service, where no local hook runs, run `mise run hooks:merge`. No hook ever blocks a push, so a branch always reaches the maintainer for review.
- Never merge, push or tag without the maintainer's go-ahead.

- **Bump with `mise run version:bump`, and know what it moves.** The substrate, the kinds in the catalogue's `[conventions.release]`, is one release, moved together and tagged once as `ontologies-vX.Y.Z` (ADR-A129). A standalone module (MORK, SPC, Surface, Persistence) and an applied module are each released on their own, with `--layer-target <module>`: all of the module's spec documents move to one number together (STD-230), its vocab documents are a unit of their own (STD-222), its shapes share one `.version` (`--with-shapes`, `--only-shapes`), and each document that moved is tagged `<name>-vX.Y.Z` (ADR-A86, ADR-A129's addendum of 2026-10-26). `mise run check:ontology-versioning -- --base-ref main` prints a `HOW` line with the command for each module it flags, and `tools/bump_version.py` holds the mechanics (CAP-105). The per-module substrate tags from before release 0.18.0 are history.

The version rules above hold in LATTICE through `mise run version:bump` and `release:prepare`: it moves every release member's shared version number forward (ADR-A129) and cascades into every applied module that pins it, and the skill `lattice-ontology-authoring` has the rest. `check:ontology-versioning` reports a pending bump for a branch's own changed content. Where a branch defers versioning, `check:ontology-versioning`'s `UNBUMPED` is expected, the release note goes under `- **Unreleased**.` in the layer's README, classed as the versioning policy says (STD-293), and the bump is made by `mise run version:bump`, for the substrate or with `--layer-target` for a module released on its own, as the check's `HOW` line says.

Whenever `mise run build:ontology-releases` adds a row, or `mise run check:ontology-versioning` lists pending tags, end the handoff with the release tags notice.

A hook runs quick checks only (ADR-A133 decision 13, STD-318). The suites are `mise run check:persistence-conformance`, which runs the generated SPARQL on every engine we have (skill `lattice-testing`), for a change to persistence, and `mise run test:config-studio-browser`, the studio's browser suites on the fake service and on a real stack the harness starts in isolation, for a change to the studio's application, services, contracts or worker. A failure on one engine is recorded in the triple-store record.

The merge gate is ADR-A133, with published decisions over the whole tree and ontology versioning among the merge checks. A README migrated to the ADR-A126 layout may cite only a published decision (ADR-A127), and the published-decisions check fails the merge on a citation of a Proposed one, so the handoff before a merge lists every Proposed decision such a README cites under 🔴 PLAN FIRST, for the maintainer to accept first (PDD-16).

## Reporting

- A handoff lists what was built, what was run and its real result, what was not run, what to check first, and every deviation from the plan with its reason.
- A "what next" report ends with 🔴 PLAN FIRST when something must be decided first, or 🟢 READY TO BRANCH when a new branch is actually due.

- A handoff names the ROADMAP.md sections it refreshed and the ones it checked and left, since every handoff attends to the roadmap (STD-307). The generated ones are `mise run build:roadmap -- --fetch`, and the hand-written ones follow the table in Picking up and finishing.

## Project overrides

Every location and command above is a value of the project's `skill_values`, and a project sets the ones it differs on. The names are `status`, `plans`, `sketches`, `review`, `validation`, `decisions`, `pending`, `debt`, `index`, `board`, `here`, `build_work`, `check_work`, `normalise_apply`, `refresh_index`, `check_identifiers`, `hooks_merge`, `plan_first`, `ready_to_branch`, `release_notice`, `trunk` and `maintainer`. The plan and the status record are the only two a project cannot do without, so their locations are never left unset.
